findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored with S3-managed keys rather than an explicit KMS key. Without a customer-managed KMS key there is no key-level access control or audit trail for the archived reports data.

The reports_archive bucket has no logging block, so access to the archived reports is not recorded. Without access logging, unauthorized reads or exfiltration of the reports cannot be detected or investigated.

Versioning is not enabled on the reports_archive bucket, so objects can be overwritten or deleted without retaining prior versions. This weakens recovery from tampering or ransomware-style destruction of the archive.

The ledger_exports bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so financial ledger exports are stored without encryption at rest and without a customer-managed KMS key for access control and audit.
The ledger_exports bucket has no logging block, so access to ledger exports is not recorded and unauthorized access cannot be detected.
Versioning is not enabled on the ledger_exports bucket, so ledger objects can be overwritten or deleted without retaining prior versions, weakening tamper detection and recovery.
The model_artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored without explicit encryption at rest or a customer-managed KMS key.

The ops_runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbooks are stored without encryption at rest. Runbooks frequently contain sensitive operational details and credentials.
The ops_runbooks bucket has no logging block, so access to runbooks is not recorded and unauthorized access cannot be detected.
